title: Vectorized backtesting SMA signals must avoid look-ahead bias
claim: Vectorized SMA crossover backtesting requires alignment: signal generation and trading decision use only data available at or before signal time
support: Chapter 4 demonstrates signal timing with explicit cutoff; early signal use inflates backtest returns
mechanism: Vectorized approach computes all SMAs, then applies crossover rule; must ensure data cutoff matches trading timestamp
assumptions: SMAs computed from historical data only
Liquid execution at close or next open

title: Vectorized backtesting assumes zero slippage and fixed commissions
claim: Vectorized backtesting simplifies: assumes zero slippage, fixed commissions, no gaps, single-candle execution; real markets differ significantly
support: Author explicitly states vectorization prioritizes speed over realism; event-based backtesting addresses gaps
mechanism: Vectorized approach applies entry/exit rules uniformly without tick-level simulation
assumptions: Entry and exit at daily close

title: Data snooping overfitting risk in parameter optimization
claim: Optimizing SMA parameters without out-of-sample validation biases results; walk-forward backtesting essential to detect overfitting
support: Chapter 4 explicitly discusses data snooping; parameter-search methods listed as high-risk without validation
mechanism: Optimizer finds parameters fitting noise; parameters fail on out-of-sample data due to regime change
assumptions: Parameters optimized on full backtest period
failure_modes: Strategy profitable in backtest, loses live

title: Linear regression for market prediction requires feature-target alignment
claim: Linear regression for future returns uses lagged price features to predict future direction; must align features (day t) with targets (day t+H) to avoid look-ahead bias
support: Chapter 5 walks through feature construction and target alignment
mechanism: Regressor learns relationship between past returns and future returns
assumptions: Prediction horizon aligns with opportunity window
failure_modes: Mean-reversion market: coefficients flip in different regime
Data leakage if target overlaps features

title: Deep neural networks risk overfitting without regularization
claim: Chapter 5 neural network example lacks explicit dropout/L1/L2 regularization or walk-forward validation; without these, models risk overfitting to noise
support: Neural network section does not mention dropout, regularization, or cross-validation; performance on training set only
mechanism: High-capacity networks memorize training data; in-sample overfitting masked by training accuracy
assumptions: Data contains robust signal above noise

title: Event-based backtesting enables tick-level simulation
claim: Chapter 6 event-driven backtester simulates order placement at each tick, allowing partial fills, limit orders, stop-loss not possible in vectorized approach
support: Chapter 6 constructs base class with event loop; long-only and long-short subclasses place orders event-by-event
mechanism: Event loop iterates ticks; at each, checks signal, places order if condition met, updates position and P&L

title: Position state machine enforces single-position invariant
claim: Long-short backtester tracks separate long/short positions; entry into new position requires closing opposite position first
support: Chapter 6 code enforces: close long first if sell signal fires; close short first if buy signal fires
mechanism: State machine: at each tick, checks position state; if opposite signal fires, closes existing before opening new
assumes: No overnight holding of both long and short

title: Oanda API uses OAuth2 REST endpoints
claim: Oanda OAuth2 authentication; REST endpoints: /instruments/candles (historical), /pricing/stream (streaming), /orders (place orders)
support: Chapter 8 walks through account setup, token generation, requests library examples
mechanism: REST + JSON; requests library handles HTTP and deserialization

title: FXCM API structure mirrors Oanda; broker now defunct
claim: FXCM API (tick, candles, streaming, orders) mirrors Oanda v20 structure; FXCM broker shut down operations; code patterns portable to other brokers
support: Chapter 9 covers FXCM endpoints: /tickdata, /candles, /orders; same REST+JSON as Oanda
mechanism: Both brokers use REST APIs; requests library handles both uniformly

title: Kelly Criterion optimal position sizing formula
claim: Kelly f* = (p*b - q) / b; for 52% win rate, 1:1 payoff, f*=4% of capital per trade maximizes long-run wealth
support: Chapter 10 derives Kelly formula; walks through binomial and stock examples
mechanism: Kelly maximizes expected log utility; lower bound avoids ruin, upper bound avoids over-sizing
failure_modes: p overstated 1-2%; Kelly 2-3x too high; catastrophic drawdown

title: Optimal leverage must be validated with realistic costs and constraints
claim: Chapter 10 ML strategy applies Kelly to compute optimal leverage (1-10x); must backtest with commissions, slippage, drawdown limits to validate
support: Chapter 10 backtests ML strategy with Kelly leverage; shows Sharpe 0.6 to 1.2 with 2x; no drawdown or commission sensitivity shown
mechanism: Higher leverage compounds returns and drawdowns; optimal Kelly assumes infinite capital
failure_modes: Commissions consume 50%+ of edge; reduce Kelly 2-3x
5x+ leverage during volatility risks margin call

title: Deployment requires configuration management and monitoring
claim: Chapter 10 case study: Oanda account, hardware, Python env, code versioning, logging, monitoring dashboard all necessary for reproducible live trading
support: Chapter 10 lists: account, hardware, Python env, code, execution, monitoring; Chapter 2 covers Docker/cloud
mechanism: Each component (account, hardware, env, code, logs) traceable; enables rollback and debugging
failure_modes: No version control; can't trace code version during loss
Monitoring down; blind to live state

title: Automated systems need circuit breakers and kill switches
claim: Chapter 10 does not mention circuit breakers; automated deployment risks runaway losses if logic/data breaks; kill switch and max-loss-per-day limits critical but absent
support: Deployment case study mentions monitoring/logging but not circuit breakers or kill switches
mechanism: Kill switch halts execution if anomalies detected; max-loss-per-day prevents drawdown spirals
failure_modes: Data gap triggers false signals; positions accumulate losses
Monitoring fails; trader unaware of doubling down
Max-loss not implemented; daily loss exceeds budget 2-3x
validation: Standard production practice; gap in book

title: Docker containers enable reproducible deployment across environments
claim: Chapter 2 recommends Docker for encapsulating Python environment, libraries, and code; ensures reproducibility across dev, staging, production
support: Chapter 2 walks through creating Ubuntu+Python Docker image; outlines container image vs instance distinction
mechanism: Dockerfile specifies base OS, dependencies, Python version; container inherits all; images portable across hardware
failure_modes: Dependency conflicts between image build and runtime
Security updates to base image require rebuild

title: Data storage trade-offs: HDF5 via TsTables is fast but proprietary; SQLite is portable
claim: Chapter 3 compares storage: pandas DataFrame pickle (fast but not queryable), TsTables HDF5 (fast, queryable, binary format), SQLite3 (portable, queryable, standard SQL)
support: Chapter 3 benchmarks read/write for OHLCV data; TsTables fastest for time-series; SQLite slower but more portable
mechanism: TsTables uses HDF5 binary format optimized for arrays; SQLite uses text-based SQL+indexes; trade-off is speed vs portability
assumes: Single-threaded access (TsTables not thread-safe for writes)
failure_modes: TsTables file corruption; binary format not human-readable
Schema change requires migration; painful in HDF5
